Jasmine — draft answers below for the tech note. I kept them concise for procurement, and marked places where Legal should expect to negotiate. Happy to expand any section.

1) Persistence of prompts/PHI artifacts:
- Default hosted behavior: we do not persist original prompts or full model outputs beyond 24 hours in primary logs. Short-term ephemeral caches (KV cache) are in-memory on the serving instance and are rotated per-request; they are not written to durable object storage by default.
- Audit logs: request metadata (timestamp, model version, token counts, route id, processing node id) are retained for 90 days for debugging and billing unless customer-configured otherwise. These metadata logs do not contain the full prompt text unless the customer opts into enhanced logging for debugging.
- Optional configurable retention: customers can opt-in to longer retention (S3) for audit purposes; this is an explicit setting and surfaces in the console/contract.

2) De-identification / Transformations:
- We provide two options: (a) customer-side preprocessing libraries and examples (recommended) and (b) a managed de-identification pipeline as a hosted preprocessor (token-based redaction or replace-with-hash) that runs in the model request path. The managed option leaves a hashed token mapping owned by the customer and retains no reversible PHI mapping on Redwood side.
- Note: nested PHI in attachments (binary files) is out-of-scope for the managed pipeline — customers should preprocess attachments or use Private deployment.

3) Data residency and Private options:
- US-only hosted routing: we can restrict processing to US regions and avoid cross-region replication.
- Private deployment: customers with high compliance needs can choose Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem install). Private deployment runs the control plane in the customer's network and the inference plane in dedicated, customer-controlled VPC subnets.
- For a subset of workloads needing air-gapped processing, we offer an appliance-based on-prem option (separate contract).

4) Auditability and logs:
- Audit log contents: event-type, user/principal id (hashed), timestamp, action (model-run, model-deploy, rollback), model id and version, model route id, token counts, outcome codes, and (only if enabled) truncated prompt hash.
- Retention defaults: 90 days for standard logs; 365 days for expanded audit (paid addon). Logs for Private deployments follow whatever the customer's retention/archival rules when deployed on-prem or in customer VPC.

Potential Legal negotiation points (flagged):
- What constitutes "storage" vs "transient" for prompts (we should clarify in BAA).
- Subprocessor list / notification cadence (we usually provide a current list and 30-day notice for changes).
- Right to access logs for audits: we can provide timeboxed read-only access/export, or run joint audit procedures.

Attachments we should send: short tech note (one-pager) + suggested BAA redline template.

-- Priyom

High level summary for Procurement:
- Default hosted: original prompt text is not retained beyond 24 hours unless customer enables enhanced logging. KV caches are ephemeral and in-memory; they are not written to durable storage.

- Residency: US-only routing available. Private deployment available for in-scope PHI workloads.
- Audit & access: standard 90-day logs; extended retention and export for audits are available as add-ons.
